After breakfast, set out on a sightseeing tour of La Candelaria, Bogotá’s historic centre.

The first part of the tour focuses on the city’s history. Walk through the old quarters, where colonial buildings, narrow streets and the capital’s main squares have been preserved.

The itinerary includes the Gold Museum. Its collection contains about 34,000 pre-Hispanic gold objects and more than 25,000 pre-Columbian exhibits. Jewellery, ceremonial pieces and other finds show what the metal meant to the cultures that lived here long before the Spanish arrived.

Next, visit Casa de la Moneda and the Botero collection, which features works by Fernando Botero, one of Colombia’s best-known painters and sculptors.

Continue to Bolívar Square, surrounded by the Cathedral, Casa de Nariño, associated with the Colombian presidency, the Liévano Palace, which houses Bogotá City Hall, and the Palace of Justice.

The day ends at Monserrate. Ascend the mountain for views of the capital and the Andes around it. Return to the hotel after the tour.
Street performers on stilts in front of a cathedral on a square in Bogotá, Colombia
Bogotá: performers in bright costumes on the square in front of the cathedral

Today you leave Bogotá to visit Lake Guatavita and the Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá.

Begin in the centre of the small town of Guatavita, where the walk takes about 15 minutes. The lake of the same name is about 10 minutes away, and a visit to the nature park usually takes 1–2 hours.

Guatavita is closely linked to the legend of El Dorado. The Muisca considered the lake sacred. According to one version of the legend, a new ruler would cover himself in gold and go out onto the lake on a raft during a ceremony, while precious objects were thrown into the water. Tales of gold and riches in the Andes later drew conquistadors and numerous expeditions to the area.

Your guide will explain how the legend evolved, why the search for El Dorado focused on this area and what attempts were made to find the supposed treasure. The route follows Indigenous trails through mountain scenery.

The second main stop is Zipaquirá, home to the famous cathedral built inside a salt mine. Return to Bogotá after the tour.
